speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your sudden vertigo, can you describe the nature of the sensation—is it a feeling of spinning, lightheadedness, or imbalance?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any associated hearing loss, tinnitus, or a feeling of fullness in your ears? Also, does changing the position of your head, such as rolling over in bed or looking up, trigger or worsen the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the spinning sensation occur specifically when you rolled over in bed or changed your head position? Also, do you have any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness on either side?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you mentioned the episode lasted about three minutes, did the vertigo start immediately upon rolling over in bed, or was there a delay before the spinning began? I also need to confirm if you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a feeling of fullness in one or both ears.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.
